newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Niugini Mining says Red Dome output falls.
newsitem.headline: Niugini Mining says Red Dome output falls.

text.p: Niugini Mining Ltd said on Thursday that gold equivalent production from its Red Dome mine in the Australian state of Queensland fell to 21,917 ounces in the second quarter ended June 30 from 26,421 in the previous quarter.
Total operating costs at the mine rose to US$291 an ounce from US$237 in the first quarter.
Niugini said the shortfall in metal production and increased costs at the mine, which is due to close early in the fourth quarter, was mainly due to lower head grades.
"Remaining production will be from lower gold, higher copper stockpiles," the company said in its quarterly report.
"Increased on-site costs resulted from increased closure cost adjustments and commencement of site cleaning campaigns in preparation for cessation of production," it said.

Niugini said gold equivalent production from its San Crisobal mine in Chile had risen to 18,340 ounces from 16,320 in the previous quarter, with total operating costs down to US$359 an ounce from US$385, due mainly to higher head grades.
The company was currently reassessing the mine plan to optimise returns by eliminating marginal material and increasing cut-off grades, it said.

In relation to its 17.5 percent stake in the Lihir gold mine in Papua New Guinea, Niugini said US$245 million of Lihir Gold Ltd's main US$300 million finance facility had been drawn by the end of the quarter.
Drawdown of the ECU25 million loan facility from the European Investment Bank was expected in the next quarter.
Lihir produced 24,126 ounces of gold in the quarter after its commissioning in May, with total sales for the quarter being 8,541 ounces of gold and 1,069 ounces of silver, it said.
